loadConsensusPeaks

Source: R/loadConsensusPeaks.R
loadConsensusPeaks.Rd

Builds the regions of an analysis from the peaks called on each sample. The peaks are combined into a consensus within each group of samples through consensusRegions, and the group consensus are pooled into a total one, which becomes the region set counted downstream. Regions supplied by the user can split the total consensus into sets, or take its place.

Usage

loadConsensusPeaks(
  sampleSheet,
  groupBy = NULL,
  technicalBy = NULL,
  technicalArguments = NULL,
  blacklist = NULL,
  greylist = NULL,
  regionSets = NULL,
  regionMode = "split",
  unassignedSet = "other",
  seqlevelsStyle = "UCSC",
  genomeAssembly = NULL,
  BPPARAM = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  weightMethod = "equal",
  calibrate = FALSE,
  nPermutations = 50L,
  targetFDR = 0.05,
  recentre = FALSE,
  width = 400L,
  combinationMethod = "stouffer",
  replicateType = "biological",
  stringencyThreshold = 1e-08,
  weakThreshold = 1e-04,
  combinedThreshold = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  minSupport = NULL,
  minReplicates = NULL,
  minOverlap = 1L,
  minOverlapFraction = NULL,
  mergeMethod = "reduce",
  maxConsensusWidth = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

sampleSheet

Data.frame returned by loadSampleSheet, or the path to a sample sheet, with at least the sample and peaks columns.

groupBy

String with the column of the sample sheet defining the groups, for instance "condition". Default: NULL, all the samples form a single group.

technicalBy

String with the column of the sample sheet naming the biological sample each library comes from, for instance "bioRep". The libraries of a group sharing a value are technical replicates: their peaks are joined first into one peak set per biological sample, which then enters the consensus of the group as a single replicate. A label found in more than one group, such as R1 in every condition, names a different sample in each of them. Default: NULL, every library is a biological replicate.

technicalArguments

Named list of arguments of consensusRegions::runConsensus, or of consensusRegions::buildConsensus, for the step joining the technical replicates, for instance list(replicateType = "biological", minReplicates = 2) to keep the peaks found in two libraries out of three. They take precedence over the ones this step inherits from the consensus of the groups. The calibration, the recentring and their arguments are reserved to the consensus of the groups. Ignored without technicalBy. Default: NULL, the arguments of the consensus of the groups, with replicateType = "technical" and equal weights.

blacklist

Regions of the assembly whose peaks must be dropped before any consensus is built, typically the list returned by loadBlacklist. Either a GRanges, a path to a BED-like file, a data.frame, or a list of them, which are pooled. The list is stored in the blacklist slot (read with blacklistRanges) of the object, as applyBlacklist does. Default: NULL.

greylist

Regions of this experiment whose peaks must be dropped before any consensus is built, typically the list built from the inputs by makeGreylist. Accepts the same forms as blacklist. Default: NULL.

regionSets

Regions of interest of the user, in any form accepted by loadRegions: a named list of paths, GRanges or data.frames. Default: NULL, the total consensus is the only set.

regionMode

String indicating what regionSets do, either "split", where every region of the total consensus goes to the first set it overlaps, or "replace", where the sets of the user are the regions and the peaks only annotate them. Ignored without regionSets. Default: "split".

unassignedSet

String with the name of the set collecting the consensus regions that overlap none of regionSets in "split" mode. NULL drops them. Default: "other".

seqlevelsStyle

String indicating the chromosome naming style, one among "UCSC", "Ensembl" or "NCBI", or NULL to keep the names as they are. Default: "UCSC".

genomeAssembly

String indicating the genome assembly to store with the regions, e.g. "hg38". Default: NULL.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallelParam object, used as it is, or a number of cores as a shorthand for one. A number of cores is shared out: the groups with more than one sample are built side by side, one worker per group, and with calibrate = TRUE the cores left over go to the calibration inside each group. A BiocParallelParam object goes to the calibration of every group when calibrate = TRUE, the groups being built one after the other, and runs the groups side by side otherwise, so that two levels of workers are never stacked. Default: NULL, a BiocParallel::SerialParam(), so that nothing runs in parallel unasked.

seed

Number seeding the random numbers of the calibration, when calibrate = TRUE. It goes to runConsensus for every group, which hands it to the BiocParallel back end of the permutations as its RNGseed, and it is stored in parameters$loadConsensusPeaks$seed, so that the consensus can be built again identically, on any number of cores. Needs consensusRegions 0.99.2 or later. Default: NULL, no seed, and a calibrated consensus may change from one call to the next.

weightMethod

String with the weights of the replicates within a group, passed to consensusRegions::computeReplicateWeights: "equal", "frip", "librarySize" or "intrinsic". "equal" counts every replicate the same and is the reproducible choice. With "frip" or "librarySize" the BAM files of the sample sheet are used. Default: "equal".

calibrate

Logical value to indicate whether the threshold on the combined p-value must be estimated within each group by consensusRegions::calibrateThreshold, against shuffled peaks, instead of being fixed by combinedThreshold. Default: FALSE.

nPermutations

Number of shuffles of the calibration. Ignored when calibrate = FALSE. Default: 50.

targetFDR

Numeric value with the empirical false discovery rate the calibration aims for. Ignored when calibrate = FALSE. Default: 0.05.

recentre

Logical value to indicate whether the consensus of each group must be reduced to windows of fixed width around the summits, as consensusRegions::recentrePeaks does. It suits transcription factors and ATAC-seq, not broad domains, and with several groups the union merges overlapping windows back into wider regions. Default: FALSE.

width

Width in base pairs of the recentred windows. Ignored when recentre = FALSE. Default: 400.

combinationMethod

String with the way the p-values of overlapping peaks are combined, one among "stouffer", "fisher", "lancaster" and "rankProduct". Default: "stouffer".

replicateType

String with the kind of replicates in a group: "biological" asks for minSupport supporting replicates, "technical" for all of them. Default: "biological".

stringencyThreshold

Numeric value with the p-value below which a peak is stringent. Default: 1e-8.

weakThreshold

Numeric value with the p-value above which a peak is taken as background and plays no further part. Default: 1e-4.

combinedThreshold

Numeric value with the threshold on the combined p-value. Its scale depends on combinationMethod, so a value chosen for one scheme does not mean the same under another. Default: NULL, stringencyThreshold is used.

alpha

Numeric value with the level of the Benjamini-Hochberg step within each replicate. Default: 0.05.

minSupport

Number of other replicates of the group that must hold an overlapping peak. Give this or minReplicates, not both. Default: NULL, one supporting replicate is enough.

minReplicates

Number of replicates of the group that must hold the peak, counting the one it came from, as a count (2), a proportion (0.66) or a percentage ("66%"), the last two rounded up. minReplicates = 2 is the same requirement as minSupport = 1. Default: NULL.

minOverlap

Minimum overlap in base pairs between two peaks for one to support the other. Default: 1.

minOverlapFraction

Minimum overlap as a fraction of the shorter of the two peaks, required on top of minOverlap. Default: NULL, no such requirement.

mergeMethod

String with the way the confirmed peaks are merged: "reduce" merges anything that touches, "iterative" keeps the most significant peak, removes what overlaps it and repeats. Default: "reduce".

maxConsensusWidth

Maximum width in base pairs of a merged region. Wider regions are rebuilt with the iterative rule. Default: NULL, no limit.

verbose

Logical value to indicate whether the messages must be printed. Default: TRUE.

...

Any other argument of consensusRegions::runConsensus or consensusRegions::buildConsensus, for instance adjustmentFamily or minSupportWeight. peaks and sampleNames come from the sample sheet and cannot be given.

Value

A RegionSetDE object. Every region carries peak.<group>, telling whether the consensus of that group overlaps it, peak.groups, the number of groups with a consensus peak on it, and peak.samples, the number of samples with a peak on it. With technicalBy, peak.samples counts the libraries and peak.biological the biological samples. The consensus slot (read with consensusData), read with consensusData, keeps the consensus of every group, the consensusRegions object behind it, the peaks of every sample after the blacklist and the greylist, the peaks they removed, the two lists, the total consensus, the table of the samples and the sample sheet itself, which countReads and countBigwig read when no file is given to them. The blacklist goes to the blacklist slot (read with blacklistRanges), the greylist to the greylist slot (read with greylistRanges) with its size in parameters$greylist, and the peaks each of them removed from every sample to the filtering.log, read with filteringLog. Where the random numbers of the calibration came from is recorded in parameters$loadConsensusPeaks, see Details.

Details

The consensus is built group by group and then pooled, rather than once over all the samples. A single requirement over all the libraries, such as a peak in at least two of them, favours the larger group, while the same requirement applied within each group treats them alike, and the union keeps the regions found in one group only. A group with a single sample has no replicate to agree with, and its peaks stand for the group as they are.

Technical replicates, given through technicalBy, are joined before the consensus of the group. The combination of consensusRegions takes every replicate as an independent piece of evidence, and two libraries of the same biological sample are not: put side by side with the other samples of the group, they would count the same sample twice, and a peak found in the two libraries of one sample alone would meet a requirement of two supporting replicates. Here the libraries of each biological sample are joined first, by default keeping the peaks found in all of them, and the peak set of every biological sample enters the consensus of its group as one replicate. That peak set carries the combined p-value of its libraries, which with the Stouffer method is close to what a peak caller would report on the pooled reads, and the summit of its most significant peak, so that recentre still has a summit to work from. The calibration, when asked for, runs on the consensus of the groups only. A biological sample with a single library keeps its peaks as they are. The consensus of every biological sample is kept in consensusData(x)$technical. Weights taken from the BAM files of the sheet, with weightMethod = "frip" or "librarySize", describe libraries rather than biological samples, and they are refused with technicalBy unless the values are given through ....

The peaks are read by consensusRegions, which keeps the standard chromosomes only, as GenomeInfoDb::keepStandardChromosomes defines them: scaffolds, patches and unplaced contigs are dropped, and so are chromosomes whose names it does not recognise.

The peaks overlapping blacklist and greylist are removed before the consensus, not after it. An artefact lying next to a genuine peak would otherwise merge with it, and removing the merged region afterwards would take the genuine peak away as well. The blacklist is applied first and the greylist to the peaks left, so a peak lying on both is counted as blacklisted. The two lists are kept apart because they say different things: a blacklist describes the assembly and is the same for every experiment, a greylist describes the inputs of this one. Both are recorded the way applyBlacklist and applyGreylist record them, so the counts, the fit and the results built from the object carry the two lists with them, and countReads leaves their reads out of the library sizes. consensusData(x)$removed holds the peaks taken out, with the sample they came from and the list that removed them, and consensusData(x)$samples their number per sample. A blacklist built for another assembly than genomeAssembly is refused, as applyBlacklist refuses it.

With regionMode = "split" the consensus regions are assigned to the sets of regionSets in the order they are given, a region overlapping two sets going to the first one. The sets then describe classes of peaks, such as promoter and distal ones, and testRegionSets can compare them. With regionMode = "replace" the counted regions are those of regionSets, and the peaks only tell which of them are occupied in each group.

The occupancy columns describe where the peaks were called, and they are a poor basis for a set of regions to test. A set of the regions found in one group only was selected on the signal of that group, so a test of its change between the groups answers a question already settled by the selection.

The consensus of a group does not depend on the other groups, so with more than one core the groups run in parallel. consensusRegions builds a consensus on a single core and only parallelises the permutations of the calibration, so without calibrate the groups are the one place where more cores save time: three groups on three cores take about as long as the largest of them. With calibrate = TRUE a number of cores is shared, divided by the number of groups for the permutations of each group. A BiocParallelParam object is never split: with calibrate = TRUE it is handed to every group as it is and the groups run one after the other, without calibration it runs the groups.

The calibration is the only step drawing random numbers: it places the peaks at random to see how often they overlap by chance. The draws come from BiocParallel, and without a seed of its own a BiocParallel back end takes them from a stream it keeps for the whole session, which a set.seed() before the call does not reset: the calibrated threshold, and with it the consensus, can then change from one call to the next. seed is passed on to consensusRegions::runConsensus in every group, which gives it to the back end of the permutations as its RNGseed: the same seed returns the same consensus whatever the number of cores, and the random numbers of the session are left as they were. Neither package calls set.seed(). parameters$loadConsensusPeaks keeps the seed and its seed.source: "seed", "BPPARAM" when a BiocParallelParam object given as BPPARAM carries its own RNGseed, which is then the one recorded, "unseeded" when the calibration ran without a seed, or "none" without calibration. A BiocParallelParam object is used as it is, so seed is ignored with it, with a warning.

See also

Examples

if (requireNamespace("consensusRegions", quietly = TRUE)) {
    peakFiles <- list.files(system.file("extdata", package = "consensusRegions"),
        pattern = "rep[0-9]\\.narrowPeak$", full.names = TRUE
    )

    # Three replicates of one condition and two of another, peaks only
    sampleSheet <- data.frame(
        sample = c("A_1", "A_2", "A_3", "B_1", "B_2"),
        bam = c("A_1.bam", "A_2.bam", "A_3.bam", "B_1.bam", "B_2.bam"),
        peaks = peakFiles[c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2)],
        condition = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B")
    )

    sampleSheet <- loadSampleSheet(sampleSheet, checkFiles = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

    regions <- loadConsensusPeaks(sampleSheet, groupBy = "condition")
    regions

    head(regionRanges(regions)$consensus, 3)

    # The same peaks split by regions of interest of the user
    firstHalf <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(1, 5e5))
    splitRegions <- loadConsensusPeaks(sampleSheet,
        groupBy = "condition",
        regionSets = list(firstHalf = firstHalf),
        verbose = FALSE
    )
    lengths(regionRanges(splitRegions))

    # Two libraries per biological sample, joined before the consensus of each condition
    libraryNames <- c("A_1a", "A_1b", "A_2a", "A_2b", "B_1a", "B_1b", "B_2a", "B_2b")
    technicalSheet <- loadSampleSheet(
        data.frame(
            sample = libraryNames,
            bam = paste0(libraryNames, ".bam"),
            peaks = peakFiles[c(1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 3, 2, 3)],
            condition = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 4),
            bioRep = rep(c("R1", "R1", "R2", "R2"), times = 2)
        ),
        checkFiles = FALSE, verbose = FALSE
    )

    technicalRegions <- loadConsensusPeaks(technicalSheet,
        groupBy = "condition",
        technicalBy = "bioRep",
        verbose = FALSE
    )
    names(consensusData(technicalRegions)$technical)
}
#> Group A: 3 samples, 292 consensus regions.
#> Group B: 2 samples, 287 consensus regions.
#> Total consensus: 292 regions from 2 groups.
#> [1] "A_R1" "A_R2" "B_R1" "B_R2"
